A Big Help to Filipinos Who Are Just Getting By: Why We Need to Talk About HB 7230

The Rental Housing Subsidy Program Act by Speaker Martin Romualdez and Tingog Partylist 🏠

There is often a massive misunderstanding when we discuss the housing situation in the Philippines. When people hear the term "informal settlers," some immediately think of a burden on society or people solely reliant on government aid. However, the reality on the ground tells a very different story.

These are the construction workers building our condos, the market vendors keeping our food affordable, the service staff, security guards, and delivery riders who keep our urban life moving. In short, they are the backbone of our daily economy, yet many of them lack secure housing.

The Solution: HB 7230

This is where House Bill No. 7230, or the proposed Rental Housing Subsidy Program Act, comes in. Authored by Speaker Martin Romualdez alongside TINGOG Partylist, this bill isn't based on mere charity - it is rooted in economic logic and social stability.

Why This Fits Our Current Situation

Housing insecurity is an economic problem. It has become too expensive to live near Central Business Districts, forcing workers to endure cramped communities just to be close to their jobs. When they are relocated to far-flung areas without livelihoods, this is what happens:

💸 Workers lose income due to high fares and long travel times.

🏢 Businesses lose their reliable workforce.

🚦 Traffic worsens and poverty cycles within the city tighten.

Through a rental subsidy, instead of relocating families to remote areas, the government helps them rent decent, safe housing near their workplaces. This protects their productivity while improving their living conditions.

How Do We All Benefit?

Some might think this is just another expense for the national treasury. However, unmanaged housing insecurity imposes hidden costs on everyone. Flooding worsens when waterways are occupied because people have nowhere else to live. Traffic intensifies, and the government ends up spending more on disaster response. Preventive housing policy is always cheaper than emergency governance.

When informal workers have stable housing:

🏙️ Cities become safer and more organized.

⛈️ Disaster risks are reduced.

🛣️ Urban infrastructure improves.

📈 The local economy grows and becomes more predictable.

The Bottom Line: #TheBlueprint

This isn't a competition over who should be prioritized - the middle class or informal settlers. We are all interconnected parts of one national workforce.

Inclusive urban development means not pushing away from opportunity the very people who build and sustain our cities. A rental subsidy gives struggling families a chance to transition toward stability. 

When communities are stable, everyone progresses toward a #BagongPilipinas. 

Housing security isn't just a handout; it is nation-building. 🇵🇭
